MAX Layout System User Guide

Chapter 4

The MAX Wire Tool

Introduction To The MAX Wire Tool

The Wire Tool facilitates drawing new wire connections. Wires can be drawn in any metal or poly layer, and include vias to switch between layers. The layers used by the Wire Tool are specified in the MAX Technology File (see Chapter 6, "MAX Technology Targeting").

The Wire Tool does not modify existing wires; however, you can delete part of an existing wire and rapidly draw new wires using the Wire Tool. You can also Stretch a segment of the wire.

Wires are drawn one at a time by entering Wire Mode, optionally selecting the layer and/or wire width, and then using the mouse to point to the wire vertices.

Starting a Wire

To create a wire, use the w hotkey or select Add Wire from the Edit Menu. This places MAX in Wire Mode, which is indicated by the mouse cursor changing to a pointing finger, and the status message (at the top of the screen) changing to wire mode.

After you enter Wire Mode, but before you start drawing the wire, you can change the layer and/or the width of the wire you will draw. If you do not select a layer, the wiring tool will use the Active Layer . If the active layer is set to auto, Auto Layer Selection will be used, meaning it will pick one of the layers under the cursor when you start drawing the wire. The active layer is specified in the palette. If there is no wireable layer under the cursor and the active layer is set to auto, the Default Layer (See Wire Setup ) from the Wire Menu is used. Alternatively, you can select a layer in one of the following ways:

  • Place the mouse over the desired layer in the palette and press mouse Button-3.
    •

  • Place the mouse over any paint in the design window, hold down Button-3 and select choose layer: <layer> from the pop-up menu. (See Figure 80).
    •

  • Change the Active Layer in the palette.
    •

  • Change the Default Layer in the Wire menu (described below).

The new layer will be reflected in the status message at the top of the screen.

    Figure 80: Wire pop-up Menu Before Wire is Started 
     

To change the wire width, use the Shift-s hotkey, or select Set Current Wire Size from the pop-up menu that appears when you press mouse Button-3 in the MAX design window. The Enter wire width form will appear (See Figure 81). If the wire width is set to 0, it means use the default wire width for the layer. The default wire width for each layer is specified in the Wiring Parameters Menu and is initialized to draw minimum width wires. You can actually change the width of the current wire segment even after you have started drawing it, but you cannot change the width of wire segments you have already completed.

    Figure 81: Edit Wire Width Form 
     

You can also set the wire width to match the width of the existing wiring layer, if any, under the cursor. To do this, press the Shift key when you start the wire (using mouse Button-1).

Drawing a Wire

To actually start drawing the wire, point the mouse to the location where you want the wire to start and press mouse Button-1 (or Shift-Button-1 to match the width of the layer under the cursor). You can then move the mouse to create the wire, which will follow the mouse movements. To create a vertex (bend in the wire) press Button-1 again. Notice that the vertex slides along the previous wire segment so that you can move the mouse in any direction and the wire will follow. To prevent the vertex from sliding, press the a key, or select anchor vertex from the pop-up menu that appears when you press mouse Button-3 (See Figure 82).

To end the wire, press mouse Button-1 over an existing metal of the same type as the wire. You can also end the wire at any time using mouse Button-2, which allows you to exit wiring mode without completing a connection. When you end the wire by completing a connection, the wire tool automatically jogs the final wire segment to make the wire align properly with the existing paint. To prevent this, end the wire by pressing the control key when you press mouse Button-1 over the wire end-point.

    Figure 82: Wire pop-up After Wire Has Been Started 
     

To change layers, drop a via using either the d or Shift-d hot keys, or use the pop-up menu on mouse Button-3. To undo a wire segment or via, use the u hot key, or select undo from the pop-up menu on mouse Button-3.

    Figure 83: Wire Tool - Dropping Vias 
     

If you are wiring in Met1 horizontally and drop a via down (hotkey: Shift-d), the via still moves in the horizontal direction (See Figure 83). In this case, you are wiring the two left gates. Having the via follow the mouse is helpful, for example, if you are trying to line up the vertical poly wire with a gate. You move the mouse over the gate and click with Button-2 on the gate and the wire and via automatically align. If you instead want to continue with poly in the horizontal direction, you must anchor the via. To do this move the via to the desired position and anchor the via (hotkey: a).

By default, the Wire Tool locks the angles to 90 degrees (Manhattan-style geometry). You can toggle between 45 degree and Manhattan with the f hotkey or by selecting the desired angle from the pop-up menu. You may also draw all-angle wires.


MAX 4.2 is only a beta release for all angle and 45 degree wires (wire paths). Interactive DRC does not work for 45 degree or all angle wires. Interactive connectivity tracing in MAX does work, but the netlist extraction does not work for 45 degree or all angle wires in this release.

Wire Menu

The Wire Menu can be entered using the Shift-w hotkey, or by selecting Wire Menu from the MAX Edit menu. It can also be entered from the pop-up menu in Wire Mode.

    Figure 84: Wire Menu 
     

Active Layer: If you are in Wire Mode and select a layer from the palette or the design window using mouse Button-3, the Active Layer is updated in this menu to reflect your layer selection.

Default Layer: The default layer is the layer that will be used if the Active Layer is set to auto and if no wireable layer is under the cursor when you start the wire.

Display Spacing Box: If selected, it displays a simple aid to wiring of a visible box around the wire as it is drawn (See Figure 85). The width of this visual box indicates the correct wire separation (as defined in the Wiring Parameters Menu ) for the current wiring layer. This is useful for spacing wires at more than the minimum width.

    Figure 85: Wire Spacing Box 
     

Snap To Grid: This option constrains all wire vertices to snap to the wiring grid for the current layer. The wiring grid for each layer is specified in the Wiring Parameters Menu , and defaults to a one micron grid.

Snap To Angle: This is the default angle constraint for wire segments, and is normally 90 degrees.

Draw Vias Using: If set to any, the code will draw vias using the first method that works: if there is a via gcell installed, that will be used; if there is a via subcell found, that will be used; as a last resort, vias will be painted using rectangles. You generally want to use the gcell option.

Via gcell name: Specify the name of gcell to use for vias, and default properties in the form: -propname value. Only used if Draw Vias Using is set to any or gcell. You can use this to specify default properties for the via, for example, to make vias symmetric by default, set it to: via -symmetric 1. You can also change this if you have created your own via gcell for use by the wiring tool.

Flylines follow mouse: If set, any flylines attached to the net being wired will follow the end of the wire. When the wire is connected, the flylines disappear.

Edit Wiring Parameters: Edit the parameters for the wiring tool. See Wiring Parameters Menu for detailed information on the wire parameters.

Wiring Parameters Menu

The Wiring Parameters Menu (See Figure 86) can be entered from the Wire Menu (obtained by using the Shift-w hotkey). This menu lets you specify the default wire widths, separation, and grid for the wires on each layer. The wire width cannot be less than the minimum allowed width for the current technology, or it is silently ignored. The grid origin is normally (0,0), but you can specify either a single number, for example 0.5, which would place the origin at (0.5,0.5), or two numbers separated by a space, for example ".5 0", which would place the grid origin at (0.5,0). The snap grid specifies the grid to snap to if snap to grid is specified in the Wire Menu. The Wire Separation is the value used for the spacing box.

    Figure 86: Wiring Parameters 
     

Wire Tool Hotkeys

Below is a summary of the hotkeys for the wiring tool. The first set of hotkeys apply after the Add Wire command (hotkey: w) and before the wire has been started.

Table 2: Hotkeys Immediately After Wire Command

Hot Key Function
Button-1 Start a minimum width wire on the active layer.
Shift- Button-1 Start a wire is same width as geometry on the active layer.
Button-2 End Wire Mode.
Button-3 Wire tool pop-up menu
b Set a spacing box to guide wiring. This is useful if your routing width is more than the minimum spacing.
f Toggle between 45/90 degree angle wiring mode
s Toggle snap to grid
Shift- s Set current wire size
Shift- w View the Wire Menu
ESC End Wire Mode

The next set of hotkeys are active after the wire has been started.

Table 3: Hotkeys During Wiring Mode

Hot Key Function
Button-1 Add a wire segment. Whenever you select Button-1, a new segment (corner) is added.
Button-2 End wire, aligned. If when you press mouse Button-2, the wire overlaps another wire of the same layer in the same direction, the wire will be automatically aligned.
Ctrl- Button-2 End wire, unaligned. The wire will end at location specified without doing any aligning.
Button-3 Wire Tool pop-up menu
a Anchor/unanchor wiring vertex or via
b Set a spacing box to guide wiring. This is useful if your routing width is more than the minimum spacing.
c Change drag via method (toggles)
d Drop a via, up one layer
Shift- d Drop a via, down one layer
f Toggle between 45/90 degree angle wiring mode
r Rotate via, if any
s Toggle snap to grid
Shift- s Set current wire size
u Undo last via or wire segment
Shift- w View the Wire Menu
x Rotate via, if any
DELETE Undo last via or wire segment
ESC End Wire Mode
(MOTION) As you move the mouse, the end of the wire segment follows the cursor. The vertex slides to follow the mouse.
